summary: Former New Mexico State Forestry lookout: a metal office chair on a wooden platform in a pine, built 1958 and removed in 1975 or 1976.

facts.design: Wooden platform near the top of a pine tree with a metal office chair; no ladder; sighting device on a stump on the ground
facts.status_note: Removed from the peak in 1976 per the register; no source describes what, if anything, remains.

events.note: Register gives 1958; the 1976 newspaper says the department had used the tower for about 20 years, which suggests an earlier start
Governor Bruce King petitioned the Legislature in 1972, 1973 and 1974 for a new 60-foot steel tower; a $37,000 bill died in committee
Staffed for only half of the 1975 season; per the 1976 newspaper, the department stopped using it the year before the story ran
Register description says removed from the peak in 1976; its details block gives 1975
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on January 1, 2026

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's description says the chair was removed from the peak in 1976 after half of the 1975 season; its details block gives 1975. The 1976 newspaper says the department stopped using it in 1975, so 1975 is the year use ended and 1976 the year it was removed. Not fully settled.
The register gives 1958, but the 1976 newspaper says the department had used the tower for about 20 years. The newspaper figure is approximate; the register date is kept.

notes_for_editor: The register's removal year is internally inconsistent: the Removed field says 1975 and the description says 1976; the 1976 newspaper says the department stopped using the chair in 1975. Story says 'removed from the peak in 1976' per the description and flags the field. Height: the newspaper gives a 34-foot pine and the register 35 feet; the record's height_m of 10.4 matches the 34-foot figure, so it was not changed. Built 1958 vs '20 years' in 1976: the newspaper figure is loose. The site's present condition is not described by any source read. The RMEF access project covers Luera Mountains state trust land and does not say whether the easement reaches the lookout site, so no access level is recorded. Two WebSearch calls were used; the register's Luera Peak photo is credited to Dixie Boyle, but no image URL was found, so no photo entry.
